text: Name a battle of the Second World War.
flavor: Some fields were ploughed again within a year. Others still give up iron every spring.
rules: Any battle, siege, campaign or named military operation of 1939 to 1945, on land, at sea or in the air. Fighting in China from 1937 counts; plans never carried out don't.

answers.lore: The largest seaborne invasion in history, on 6 June 1944. The D simply stands for day.
The first great campaign fought entirely in the air, in the summer and autumn of 1940.
Men fought floor by floor for single buildings. One, Pavlov's House, held out for two months.
Asked to surrender at Bastogne in December 1944, General McAuliffe sent back one word: Nuts!
Codebreakers confirmed the target was Midway by having the island report, falsely, that its water plant had failed.
Hundreds of little ships, from fishing boats to pleasure cruisers, helped carry more than 338,000 troops off the beaches in 1940.
Churchill wrote: before Alamein we never had a victory; after Alamein we never had a defeat.
Remembered for the photograph of six marines raising the flag on Mount Suribachi in February 1945.

aliases: German invasion of the Soviet Union
answers.lore: Named after Frederick Barbarossa, a medieval emperor said to sleep under a mountain until Germany needs him.
A gamble to end the war by Christmas 1944 by seizing Dutch bridges. The last, at Arnhem, proved a bridge too far.
It lasted nearly 900 days. Supplies came across frozen Lake Ladoga, on the Road of Life.
The ancient abbey on the hilltop, founded by Saint Benedict, was flattened by Allied bombers in 1944.

aliases: Second Battle of the Philippine Sea

answers.lore: In 1943 RAF Lancasters attacked German dams with Barnes Wallis's bouncing bombs.
After the battle in 1939 the damaged Graf Spee was scuttled off Montevideo rather than face the British ships her captain believed were waiting.

aliases: Last battle of the battleship Bismarck

answers.answer: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

answers.lore: In 1942 an old destroyer packed with explosives was rammed into the great dock gates at St Nazaire. Hours later it blew up, wrecking the dock.
In 1943 British intelligence let a dead man carrying fake invasion plans wash up in Spain. The Germans believed them.
In April 1942 sixteen army bombers took off from an aircraft carrier to strike Tokyo. None could land back on board.
The cliff on Okinawa where the unarmed medic Desmond Doss is credited with saving about 75 men in 1945.
An emergency plan for Germany's Replacement Army, set in motion by the plotters of 20 July 1944 after Stauffenberg's bomb. Hitler lived, and it collapsed by nightfall.
Norwegian commandos wrecked the heavy-water plant at Vemork in 1943, setting back Germany's atomic research.
German glider troops snatched Mussolini from a mountain hotel on the Gran Sasso in 1943.

aliases: Arctic convoys of World War II

answers.answer: Sinking of Prince of Wales and Repulse
aliases: Sinking of HMS Prince of Wales
Battle of the Gulf of St Lawrence
Battle of Mariana and Palau Islands

answers.lore: In April 1940 an old Norwegian fortress, its cannons nicknamed Moses and Aaron, sank the German cruiser Blücher.

answers.answer: Battle of the Santa Cruz Islands
aliases: Battle for the Santa Cruz Islands

answers.lore: In 1943 some 34,000 Allied troops stormed Kiska, in the Aleutians. The Japanese had slipped away weeks before.
A secret war of radio beams that guided German bombers to British cities, and of British efforts to bend them.
In May 1945 American and German soldiers fought side by side to defend an Austrian castle, and its French VIP prisoners, from the SS.
In February 1942 jittery gunners fired over 1,400 anti-aircraft shells into the sky above Los Angeles. There was no enemy.
Three days into the war, in September 1939, RAF fighters shot down two RAF Hurricanes by mistake.

traps.reason: A battle of the First World War.
A war of its own, though its battles count.
A whole theatre of the war, not one battle.
An atrocity against the defenceless, not a battle.
A forced march of prisoners, not a battle.
A plan never carried out.
A secret programme to build the bomb, not a battle.
A war of codes, fought at desks rather than on a battlefield.
A hunt for German scientists after the fighting, not a battle.
A breakout from a prison camp, not a battle.
A conference, where the war's end was argued over, not fought.
A day of victory, not a battle.
A long, uneasy lull, with barely any fighting in the West.
A way of fighting, not a battle.
From another war.
A battle of fiction. Navarone was invented for the novel.
The film's raid is fiction, though the prisoners' railway bridge was real.
A brawl between Allied servicemen in 1942, not a battle.
A railway forced out of prisoners of war, not a battle.
A truce of the First World War, not a battle.
A battle of the Napoleonic Wars, fought in 1813.
A bomber or a bomb, not a battle. Name the attack itself.

source: Copied from the daily question "ww2-battles" on 28 November 2026.
